result.summary: Adds stream output `operator<<` overloads for common Bitcoin Core types in a test utility (`src/test/util/common.{h,cpp}`) so test frameworks can format them. Converts equality assertions across 15 unit test files from bare `BOOST_CHECK` to `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL` and `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS`, printing actual versus expected values when assertions fail.
result.problem: When unit test assertions using `BOOST_CHECK(a == b)` fail, Boost only outputs a boolean failure without displaying the mismatched values. Many internal types (such as `FeeFrac`, `CScript`, `CAddress`, and `CTxDestination`) lacked stream insertion operators in the test harness, preventing developers from seeing failure diagnostics without extra debugging code.
evidence: PR description: 'If the `<<` operator exists, boost can use this as a debug output when a check fails (besides `BOOST_CHECK`). This adds `<<` for types commonly used across the unit tests that do not yet have a display output. Each callsite that uses these types are then updated to use macros that will print the debug output on failure.'

PR description notes that the formatting overloads also prepare for removing Boost test runner: 'All of these display strings would be used as part of #35713, but we can also use them with boost today.'
result.scope_notes: A mechanical test-only refactor spanning 15 unit test files, converting equality assertions to value-printing macros alongside new test-only `operator<<` definitions.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor updates to callsites and operator overloads.
result.card: This PR adds stream output operator<< overloads for common Bitcoin Core data types in test utilities and migrates assertions across unit test suites from BOOST_CHECK to BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL. Unit test assertion failures previously reported only a boolean false without displaying the mismatched values, complicating failure diagnosis. The changes also provide string representations needed by the proposed migration away from Boost unit test runner in PR 35713.

risk.why: Touches only unit test utilities and assertions; errors would cause test build or diagnostic failures with no impact on release binaries.
